ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $CD$ is the altitude from the right angle of $\triangle ABC$ to the hypotenuse $AB$. By folding $\triangle BCD$ along $CD$ such that point $B$ coincides precisely with the midpoint $E$ of $AB$, what is the measure of $\angle A$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $\triangle BCD$ is folded along CD, \\
it follows that $BC = CE$, \\
since E is the midpoint of AB and $\angle ACB=90^\circ$, \\
it follows that $CE = BE = AE$, \\
thus, $\triangle BEC$ is an equilateral triangle, \\
hence, $\angle B = 60^\circ$, \\
therefore, $\angle A = 90^\circ - 60^\circ = \boxed{30^\circ}$

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, AB is a horizontal line, A is at the left end, and B is at the right end; E and D are located on AB, in the order A, E, D, B. Point C is above D, and CD is a vertical line segment; in the figure there is a shaded triangle CDE, and the dashed lines on the right from C to B and from D to B represent triangle BCD before folding; after folding, B coincides with the midpoint E of AB. Reasoning: When folding along CD, C and D remain unmoved on the crease, and point B is mapped to point E, so line segment CB is mapped to CE; therefore BC = CE. Also because E is the midpoint of the hypotenuse AB of right triangle ABC, according to the theorem of the midpoint of the hypotenuse of a right triangle, EA = EB = EC. Thus, in triangle BEC, BE = EC, and from the folding BC = EC, so BE = EC = BC. Therefore triangle BEC is an equilateral triangle, and ∠CBE = 60°. Since E is on AB, ray BE has the same direction as BA, so ∠CBE is ∠ABC. Triangle ABC is right-angled at C, therefore ∠A + ∠B = 90°, so ∠A = 90° - 60° = 30°.
